items.text: Care for your children while you are strong, for they will care for you when you are old.
items.quote: the trouble which parents bestow upon their helpless children when they are themselves vigorous is repaid to them in old age when they are helpless by their children

items.text: Repay your parents' care: support them in old age when they are helpless.
items.quote: is repaid to them in old age when they are helpless by their children, who are then in their full vigour

items.text: Do not wrong your wife, especially by forming connections outside your own house.
items.quote: the avoidance of doing her any wrong... wrong inflicted by a husband is the formation of connexions outside his own house

items.text: Do not approach one another with false affectation in person or in manners.
items.quote: husband and wife ought not to approach one another with false affectation in their person any more than in their manners

items.text: Acquire possessions outside the house for the household.
items.quote: that the one may acquire possessions outside the house, the other preserve those within

items.text: Preserve within the house what your husband acquires.
items.quote: that the one may acquire possessions outside the house, the other preserve those within

items.text: Educate your children.
items.quote: the woman by nurturing, the man by educating them

items.text: Nurture your children.
items.quote: the woman by nurturing, the man by educating them

items.text: Cooperate with one another to secure not merely existence but a good life.
items.quote: the female and the male co-operate to ensure not merely existence but a good life

items.text: Provide yourself with good slaves, and carefully bring up those to whom the higher duties are to be entrusted.
items.quote: provide oneself with good slaves... bring up carefully those to whom the higher duties are to be entrusted.
items.conflict: Treating persons as property conflicts with the biblical teaching that all are made in God's image and that slave-trading is a sin (Exod 21:16; 1 Tim 1:10).

items.text: Do not allow your slaves to be insolent, and do not irritate them.
items.quote: The intercourse of a master with his slaves should be such as not either to allow them to be insolent or to irritate them.

items.text: Give the higher class of slaves a share of honor, and give the workers abundant nourishment.
items.quote: To the higher class of slaves he ought to give some share of honour, and to the workers abundance of nourishment.

items.text: Never give wine to slaves, or at any rate very seldom.
items.quote: wine ought never to be given to slaves, or at any rate very seldom.

items.text: Give slaves work and sufficient food; do not give food without work and punishment, nor work and punishment without food.
items.quote: It remains therefore to give them work and sufficient food; for it is impossible to rule over slaves without offering rewards, and a slave's reward is his food.

items.text: Bestow or withhold food, clothing, leisure, and punishments according to merit.
items.quote: we must take careful notice and bestow or withhold everything, whether food or clothing or leisure or punishments, according to merit

items.text: Offer slaves their freedom as a prize, and define a limit of time for their service.
items.quote: it is just and beneficial to offer slaves their freedom as a prize... and a limit of time is defined

items.text: Bind slaves to your service by the pledges of wife and children, and do not keep many persons of the same race in one household.
items.quote: One ought to bind slaves to one's service by the pledges of wife and children, and not to have many persons of the same race in a household
items.conflict: It uses family ties to hold persons in bondage and denies the liberty and equality of all in Christ (Gal 3:28; 1 Cor 7:21-23).

items.text: Provide sacrifices and pleasures more for the sake of slaves than for freemen.
items.quote: One ought to provide sacrifices and pleasures more for the sake of slaves than for freemen
items.conflict: Offering sacrifices conflicts with the exclusive worship of God through Jesus Christ; idolatrous offerings are forbidden (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Arrange the house for the health and well-being of its inhabitants; make it airy in summer and sunny in winter.
items.quote: The house must be arranged both with a view to one's possessions and for the health and well-being of its inhabitants... airy in summer and sunny in winter.

items.text: Rise earlier than your slaves and retire later; leave nothing undone whether day or night, and keep the house guarded.
items.quote: masters ought to rise earlier than their slaves and retire to rest later, and a house should never be left unguarded

items.text: Attend to the sphere allotted to you in the household economy, and let her attend to hers.
items.quote: Some things should be attended to by the master, others by his wife, according to the sphere allotted to each in the economy of the household.
